transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... for months now, I've been seeing this exact same pattern. My sister’s appointments keep getting moved around, bills show up wrong, and people just conveniently forget to call me back. 

Everyone keeps telling me it’s just clerical mistakes, but... I know what I'm seeing. They’re deliberately keeping information from me and trying to push me out of making decisions.
Aside from these suspicions about people around you, have you ever heard voices or sounds, or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see?

No, nothing like that. I don't hear voices or... see things that aren't there. 

I'm not imagining this. Everything I'm talking about is right there in front of me—the paper trails, the schedules, the actual bills. It's real, tangible things that are happening, not my mind playing tricks on me.
Have you generally been a mistrustful or suspicious person throughout your life, even before this situation started, or is this the first time you've felt this way about people?

No, I wouldn't say that at all. I've actually always been a pretty trusting person. I mean, I've worked as an office supervisor for years, and you have to rely on your team and trust people to do their jobs. I've never had a reason to doubt people like this before. 

It's really just... well, it's just recently, with my sister's situation, that all this started happening. This is the first time I've ever had to deal with people actively doing things like this to me.
Can you tell me exactly how many months this has been going on since you first started noticing this pattern with your sister's situation?

It's been about 11 months now. That was right around the time my sister's health suddenly took a turn for the worse, and I had to step in and start coordinating all of her care. That's exactly when I started noticing all of this happening.

latest_inference.note: The absence of hallucinations, the isolated and non-bizarre nature of the persecutory beliefs (limited to the sister's care situation), preserved prior personality and occupational functioning, and a clear, single-theme delusional system persisting for ~11 months strongly support Delusional Disorder rather than Schizophrenia (which requires additional symptoms like hallucinations, disorganization, or negative symptoms) or Other Psychotic Disorder (F28), which is reserved for atypical presentations not fitting a specific category.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that family/associates are deliberately withholding information and manipulating schedules/bills to exclude her from decision-making) that has persisted for approximately 11 months. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech, and no negative symptoms, arguing against schizophrenia (F20). The delusional belief is circumscribed to this specific persecutory theme, with otherwise preserved reality testing, insight into the absence of hallucinations, and intact occupational functioning (still working as an office supervisor), consistent with Delusional Disorder rather than a broader psychotic process. The patient explicitly denies a lifelong pattern of suspiciousness or mistrust predating this episode, with acute onset tied to a specific stressor (sister's illness), arguing against Paranoid Personality Disorder (F60.0). Duration exceeds the 1-month threshold required for F22 and the delusion is non-bizarre and thematically coherent (persecutory type), fitting F22 criteria well.
